bullets.note: Bullet text sits inside the company or project title margin, wrapped lines align under the first text line, and the marker is lowered to the text baseline in both DOCX and PDF. An engagement title aligns with the role bullet text and its own bullets sit one level deeper, giving three visible depths: employer, named project, achievement. Both renderers consume these tokens; neither infers indentation from a viewer default.

summary.note: Use three to five complete sentences with a 90-word ceiling. The first sentence states the exact confirmed professional identity and N+ years of experience from the confirmed, non-overlapping employment timeline as of the application date. Every later sentence must add a distinct career-level signal; never restate the identity as a framework-specific title or repeat the opening in different words. Prefer architecture, performance, testing, delivery, production support, product scope, or domain breadth over internal implementation terminology. Relocation renders as a separate header line and is not repeated here. The summary is the only place a cross-project fact can live, because a bullet describes one project. Do not pad a sentence or invent context to reach the minimum.

page_length.note: Prefer one page for a confirmed career span of up to five years. A second page is available for longer careers when relevant evidence needs it; it is not a target. Years-of-experience wording is recalculated from the confirmed profile timeline and validated separately.

career_breaks.note: Career breaks are optional explanatory context, not an automatic section. Include one only when it materially resolves a recent or otherwise conspicuous timeline question that the visible employment dates cannot answer, or when the target context makes the explanation directly useful. A broad year-only label that still leaves the exact transition unclear fails the marginal-value test. On a constrained page, prefer stronger target-relevant Experience evidence and omit the section unless its explanatory value is greater.

contact_hygiene.note: The confirmed professional title renders between the name and contact row. With automatic hyperlinks enabled, every included email or profile entry that has a recorded URL must render that URL behind its human-readable label; omission is a validation error. Phone remains a literal unlinked number. The validation report flags missing contact categories but does not invent them. Use a professional personal email address; do not use a previous employer address. Location and work authorization belong in the header only when relevant and confirmed in profile.yaml.

mobility.note: Use one concise plain-text relocation phrasing confirmed in profile.yaml. Prefer a confirmed target-specific destination, never infer one from the job, and do not repeat the line in the summary.

languages.note: Prefer CEFR levels for European applications. A missing level is a warning, not an automatic conversion: the user's recorded proficiency must be preserved until they confirm a CEFR mapping. Never render visual skill bars or stars.

delivery.note: Rendering keeps stable resume.docx and resume.pdf files for tooling and also writes professionally named attachment copies derived only from the confirmed name and target role.

job_targeted_content_balance.summary_lead: Begin with the exact confirmed profile professional title. Append the advertised discipline, framework, or specialization when eligible evidence supports it; never replace the profile identity with a framework-first target label.
job_targeted_content_balance.customer_facing_experience: When the target asks for customer-facing apps and eligible evidence exists in a current or highly relevant role, retain at least one concrete product, UI, or user-workflow bullet. Authentication, infrastructure, release, and CI/CD evidence must not occupy every bullet.
job_targeted_content_balance.distinct_integrations: When the posting explicitly requests payments or another third-party integration, retain a distinct implementation when it adds a materially different gateway, trust boundary, or failure model.
job_targeted_content_balance.engagement_marginal_value: A named engagement pays for both a heading and its bullets. Remove it when its only incremental value is architecture, framework, or keyword wording already visible in Summary, Skills, Freelance Projects, or another Experience bullet. Retain a one-bullet engagement only when it adds a distinct product, ownership, platform, integration, release, scale, measured, or user-workflow signal. Prefer a stronger second bullet under the highest-ranked relevant existing engagement when that adds more value.
job_targeted_content_balance.note: Semantic selection gates applied before layout cuts. They exist because a layout pass cuts by length and has no idea which bullet answered the posting's main question.

links.note: Every live hyperlink is explicitly blue and underlined in DOCX and PDF so a reader can recognize it without hovering. Contact and profile targets stay behind human-readable labels. TXT has no annotation layer, so it preserves the labels and omits the targets instead of exposing raw addresses.

emphasis.note: Bold is real character formatting, which every ATS parser discards harmlessly along with the rest of the run properties. Generic product and UI nouns are excluded because bolding words such as screen or app adds no recruiting signal. The cap exists for the human reader: past roughly a dozen terms nothing stands out any more.

writing_style.note: Public resume text must use direct engineering language and plain punctuation. Replace forbidden symbols with a full stop, colon, comma, parentheses, or ASCII hyphen. Replace generic terms with the concrete feature, action, constraint, or verified result. This list is a default, not a doctrine: edit it. The em dash and en dash are here because they are the most reliable visual tell of generated text in a document nobody expects to be typeset.

selected_projects.note: The model keeps the stable `projects` field, but it renders as Freelance Projects. Default to the single strongest independent project only when it adds evidence beyond Experience. Add a second only when it contributes material, non-redundant target coverage that is stronger than the available Experience detail. Employer and academic projects are ineligible, and the section may be empty when no suitable independent work exists. Each entry must resolve to exactly one project through its source references.

quantifier_quality.note: Public resume text must not present test cases, test files, test-code size, source-code lines, source files, or commit counts as achievements. These counts are easy to change by splitting code, tests, files, or commits and do not explain engineering value. Describe the structural change, delivered capability, tested behaviors, boundaries, failure paths, determinism, or release risk instead. Other verified numbers still need to be materially meaningful and resistant to trivial manipulation.

bullet_quality.note: Applies to every engineering stack. Select and order evidence in Outcome > Impact > Scope > Activity order so the strongest bullet is first. Activity is an audit classification, not a publishable level: cut it or select stronger evidence. A bullet is one short sentence and one defensible achievement: begin with the contribution or engineering change, then state its verified consequence or meaningful scope, and keep only the technical details needed to distinguish the work. Lead at recruiter-readable professional impact and add implementation detail only when it proves an important skill, keyword, constraint, or technical result. A supported number earns space only when it materially strengthens the achievement; small adoption figures, build counts, and operational counts that read as routine or unimpressive should remain private. Reject repeated capabilities even when their implementation differs, and never add a weak bullet merely to fill the page. Do not force a result clause when no outcome is supported, and do not turn a record into a comma-separated inventory. Schema-version 2 records the A-H semantic review and metric decision for every public bullet; the executable validator requires an exact review-to-bullet and review-to-evidence match.

number_format.note: Use digits for quantities in Summary, Experience, and Freelance Projects. Preserve established punctuation such as 50,000+, 7,500+, 99.9%, and 40%. Names and official credential titles are not rewritten.

ai_experience.note: Core engineering skills remain primary. Include an AI tool only when confirmed profile or project evidence supports genuine use and the term helps the role. When AI appears in Skills, prefer one supported achievement in Summary, Experience, or Freelance Projects that shows how it contributed to delivery, investigation, prototyping, automation, or another engineering result. The renderer warns when AI is visible only as a skill keyword.

proofreading.note: Run a dedicated proofreading pass over source text and extracted DOCX/PDF text. Reject known merged-word typos, missing punctuation inside compounds, duplicated words, and rendered word-boundary changes before delivery.

protected_phrases: customer and store pickup order lifecycle
line_wrap.note: Keep complete technical and product phrases on one rendered line. Add job vocabulary here when a phrase would become ambiguous or look broken if its words wrap separately. Validation rejects a configured phrase that crosses a PDF line boundary.

content_density.note: A one-page resume that uses less than 99 percent of the printable height is underfilled. Job-targeted and master resumes should both aim to use at least 99 percent when strong, non-redundant evidence and confirmed compact sections can do so without clipping or weakening section rhythm. Restore strong relevant Experience detail first, then add a relevant independent project or compact confirmed section. Do not pad with generic prose, weak skills, certificates chosen only for length, or gameable counts.

experience_budget.note: A flat employer block gives every project inside a role the same three or four slots, so a role covering many distinct client deliverables cannot show them. Job-targeted resumes use one or two role-framing lines beside engagements. A master resume may use up to four distinct company-level or recurring-responsibility bullets before the named engagements, and up to four bullets for a substantial historical contract, when each adds a separate signal. Role-level bullets describe the experience itself; project achievements stay under their named engagements. Every added engagement or bullet must pass a resume-wide marginal-value test: keyword repetition already visible in Summary, Skills, Freelance Projects, or another achievement is insufficient. Treat the engagement heading itself as page cost. If removing a one-bullet engagement leaves its capability visible elsewhere, reject it unless the bullet adds a distinct product, ownership, platform, integration, release, scale, measured, or user-workflow signal. Prefer complementary achievements under the highest-ranked relevant existing engagement over several weak one-bullet engagements; use a confirmed public link only as a tiebreaker between otherwise comparable evidence. A single-screen repair, isolated widget, local overflow fix, package pin, or narrow bug fix is normally ineligible for a scarce Experience bullet when broader eligible product-flow, integration, multi-surface, reusable-system, measured, or delivery evidence exists. Run a separate career-strength audit so literal requirement coverage does not crowd out a higher-ranked relevant ownership, productization, adoption, scale, or sustained-delivery record. The maxima are editorial targets enforced as warnings, not structural limits; the schema bounds are wider on purpose so a genuinely dense role is not truncated.

_readme: Layout, ATS structure, and writing policy for generated resumes. Every value here is a default you may change. The renderer and the source checker both read this file, so a change takes effect in DOCX, PDF, and validation at once.
